subject: Operational runbook for DTIA evidence staging and transfer controls
messages:
From: Claire O'Neill <cla@healthcore.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@healthcore.com
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: runbook + staging workflow for DTIA evidence

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Legal has asked us to hand off an operational runbook that describes how Redwood will stage and deliver DTIA evidence for HealthCore's UK pilot. Specifically we need: 

- A short runbook describing the staging environment, retention window, and how you collect request/response audit logs (format and location).
- Details on subprocessors involved in the staging flow and any access controls (who can access logs).
- A pragmatic timeline for a 2-week evidence sprint and a proposed SFTP handoff for bulk artifacts.

I've attached HealthCore's evidence template (see dtia-evidence-reqs.xlsx) — legal marked columns in red where they need vendor input. Can you confirm if Redwood can: 

1) Stage artifacts on an SFTP/S3 bucket for 30 days?
2) Provide HMAC-signed manifests for each delivery?
3) Supply copies of the signing keys or attestations for subprocessors?

If those are possible, please send a short runbook and an estimated delivery schedule by Friday so we can align with procurement. Happy to set a quick 30-min sync if helpful.

Best,
Claire
Director, InfoSec Ops
HealthCore Medical

[attachment: dtia-evidence-reqs.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Claire O'Neill <cla@healthcore.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: runbook + staging workflow for DTIA evidence

Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for highlighting the red fields. Taking this on. High-level answers up front:

- Yes, we can stage artifacts on an S3-compatible staging bucket with an SFTP gateway for 30 days (configurable). We typically use time-based lifecycle policies and object locking where needed.
- We can produce HMAC-signed manifests per-delivery and include SHA256 checksums for every artifact.
- We cannot export Redwood service private keys, but we can provide signed attestations from our KMS (key handle, signing algorithm, timestamp) and subprocessors can provide their own attestations.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will attach a written runbook (runbook-draft-v1.md) describing the staging bucket, retention policy, manifest format, and access control matrix.
2) Kimberly and Laura will confirm legal/compliance items (SCCs vs UK IDTA applicability for HealthCore).
3) We will provision a temporary SFTP endpoint and share creds with your SFTP Support contact for a single test delivery.
4) Target: test delivery by Tue 2027-11-16; full 2-week sprint kickoff on 2027-11-20.

Small clarifications needed from HealthCore:
- Are you expecting the artifacts to include complete PII or redacted subsets? (impacts sampling and retention)
- Do you require continuous audit streaming (syslog/forwarded events) or is batch delivery acceptable?

I'll attach the draft runbook and the typical manifest template now. If that timeline looks tight, we can shift the kickoff a week.

Thanks — Logan
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

[attachment: runbook-draft-v1.md]

From: Kimberly Park <kim@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire O'Neill <cla@healthcore.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: runbook + staging workflow for DTIA evidence

Looping in legal notes for the runbook — quick observations: 

- SCCs vs UK IDTA: HealthCore is UK-entity downstream; we should include dual-path language. For EU-resident data flows we default to SCCs + appropriate technical safeguards; for UK-resident data include the UK IDTA addendum language in the runbook and reference the signed UK addendum (if not already executed).
- TIA/DTIA scope: confirm whether HealthCore considers the staging bucket a "transient processor" environment (we typically treat it as processor-accessible ephemeral storage). If so, mark any subprocessors accessing the bucket as transient and only provide attestations, not key material.
- Subprocessor attestations: we need a short template that subprocessors will sign confirming limited access and retention controls. We cannot provide raw private keys — per our KMS policy — but we can provide signed attestations and HSM/KMS audit logs extracts for the relevant window.

Action items for us:
- Logan: add a short section in the runbook titled "Legal controls & transfer mechanism mapping" with a bullet list for EU vs UK pathways and a reference to the TIA/DTIA artifacts.
- Laura: prepare a subprocessor attestation template and redline HealthCore's dtia-evidence-reqs.xlsx where legal asks for attestation language.

I'll review the runbook draft and aim to send legal redlines by EOD Monday.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Claire / HealthCore legal —

Thanks — quick update and final list of action items so folks have a single source of truth before the test delivery: 

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Runbook (Logan) — finalize runbook-draft-v1.md with legal mapping section and manifest schema. ETA: 2027-11-14 09:00 PT.
- Subprocessor attestation template (Laura) — provide template and example signed attestation. ETA: 2027-11-15 EOD.
- Provision SFTP staging endpoint (Infra/Logan) — endpoints & one-time credentials to be sent to SFTP Support on 2027-11-15.
- Test delivery (HealthCore) — perform a small sample delivery to the SFTP endpoint (one manifest + 3 artifacts). Target test window: 2027-11-16 10:00–12:00 PT.
- Evidence delivery sprint plan (Joint) — two-week cadence starting 2027-11-20 if test successful.

Notes:
- Retention: artifacts will be retained 30 days in the staging bucket by default; we can enable object-lock for a 90-day legal hold if required (requires exec signoff).
- Transfer mechanisms: runbook will include an "Escalation & fallback" section (SCCs -> UK IDTA mapping; fallback to encrypted batch S3 export if SFTP is blocked).
- Audit exports: we will provide aggregated KMS/HSM attestations and a timeboxed audit log extract (CSV) for the sprint window. Full streaming telemetry requires an extended engagement.

Please confirm the test delivery window and whether HealthCore wants PII redaction in the sample artifacts. If yes, confirm the redaction standard (masked or tokenized).

I'll circulate the runbook link once the file is finalized.

— Logan
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
